scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Move your mouse a little, and the cursor glides across the screen. There's no ball inside anymore. So how does it know?

scenes.name: light
scenes.text: Flip it over. A small light, red or invisible infrared, shines down at the surface beneath it.

scenes.name: camera
scenes.text: Next to it is a tiny camera sensor. It takes thousands of very low resolution pictures every second.

scenes.name: compare
scenes.text: A chip compares each picture with the last one. The tiny bumps and fibres of the surface shift, revealing which way and how far you moved.

scenes.name: send
scenes.text: It sends those movements to the computer, which moves the cursor to match, many times a second.

scenes.name: dpi
scenes.text: DPI is how many dots the cursor moves for each inch you move the mouse. Higher DPI means a faster cursor.

scenes.name: glass
scenes.text: On a shiny glass desk there's almost no texture to see, so many mice struggle. A mouse pad fixes that.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Light, camera, compare, cursor. Tracking every move. Follow for more on how things really work.
